sceneFacts.shortVersion: Bradley Cooper based his chef character on three real celebrity chefs.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Bradley Cooper based his character, Adam Jones, on a combination of three celebrity chefs. To prepare for the role, Cooper spent time with Marcus Wareing, Gordon Ramsay, and Marco Pierre White, incorporating their physical characteristics and "little things" into his performance. Consultant chef Marcus Wareing observed that Cooper, having just played a Navy SEAL, commanded the kitchen like a soldier.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Uma Thurman plays a food critic with a shifting British accent.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Uma Thurman portrays Simone, a food critic in the film. Her character speaks with a posh British accent that occasionally shifts to American. Simone's portrayal includes a dry personality and some funny lines.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Sienna Miller trained extensively to portray Helene as a real chef.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Sienna Miller aimed to portray her character, Helene, as a "very real person," choosing not to wear makeup or act in an inauthentic way. She observed that women working in male-dominated kitchens "have to be really tough and strong." Consultant chef Marcus Wareing praised Miller's dedication, stating she "didn’t want to be seen to act like a cook, she wanted to be a cook." Wareing added that Miller "put in so much effort and came to my kitchen on many occasions off her own back, in her own time."

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Actors cooked for real in a functioning kitchen alongside real chefs.
sceneFacts.longDescription: The kitchen set for the film was a fully functioning kitchen, designed to be picked up and moved into any real restaurant. Consultant chef Marcus Wareing ensured the cast genuinely cooked during filming. To enhance realism and pressure, some extras were actual Michelin-starred chefs from London. Wareing even turned the stoves on full to make the actors hot and sweaty.

sceneAnchor.anchorElement: All food preparation scenes were done for real, with genuine chefs sometimes acting as extras to add pressure to the actors during filming.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Bradley Cooper trained to act and cook like a real chef.
sceneFacts.longDescription: To prepare for his role as Adam Jones, Bradley Cooper and other core actors were taught to cook and act like professional chefs by consultant Marcus Wareing. Wareing observed that top actors like Cooper could embody the role, even learning to wear chef whites authentically. Cooper already possessed some cooking experience, which helped him portray the aggressive chef. Furthermore, all food preparation scenes in the movie were filmed with actual cooking to ensure realism.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Burnt's opening was 4th worst for 3,000+ theater films.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Released in over 3,000 theaters, "Burnt" earned just over $5 million on its opening weekend, placing sixth overall. This made its opening numbers the fourth worst on record for a film playing in that many theaters.
